# Tailwind styling

## Browser check repairs (2026-11-12)

Field focus uses the shared two-pixel outline. The later generic focus rule that
changed field borders and fills has been removed, keeping search focus on its
wrapper and preserving Contacts autofill paint. This is an intentional focus
behavior correction; resting controls retain their existing appearance.

Workspace access-refresh events request fresh server entitlements even when a
quota poll is pending or unavailable. Downgrades retain the saved theme preference
while falling back; restored Premium access reapplies that preference. Tooltips
reposition after ancestor entrance animations and hover transitions finish.

Browser matrices set preferences in storage before navigation, without accumulating
initialization scripts. Measurements wait for fonts, finite animations and actual
content; allowance bar ratios are polled until their animation reaches its target.
Assertions follow the current template editor navigation, appearance-specific
tutorial corners, layered Premium surfaces and scoped legacy allowances. Deletion
interception distinguishes confirmation submissions from status polling and checks
retryable errors, disabled pending controls and delayed sign-out. Background
sending-status polls authenticate without redirecting when access is revoked, so
they cannot interrupt the deletion confirmation delay or lose `/?deleted=1`. The
launch-controls test forces a poll during that delay. Tutorial close restores focus
after React commits the dialog removal and launcher visibility, avoiding a frame
callback that could run while the launcher was still hidden.

Playwright writes an HTML report, failure screenshots and retained failure traces.
CI uploads the report and results even when browser verification fails. Screenshot
tolerances, accessibility rules and the serial worker configuration are unchanged.

Additional accessibility corrections darken the Lavender/Nightbloom primary
action gradient while retaining white labels (the limiting endpoint now exceeds
4.5:1). Chalk History uses the semantic warning ink for thin queued progress
arcs and segments, exceeding 3:1 on its light surfaces. Other Chalk queued
indicators retain their chosen bright yellow. The numeric audit now interpolates
translucent gradient stops with premultiplied alpha, matching CSS rather than
inventing a bright gray midpoint. Accessibility thresholds remain unchanged.

Mobile Privacy passed against all four existing references without replacement.

## Timer ring, Premium shine and allowance outlines (2026-11-12)

The landing timer's drop-shadow now belongs to a full-size HTML wrapper around
the SVG. Rotation remains on the SVG; the centered countdown stays outside the
shadow wrapper. The panel tilt, floating animation, reveal, progress and palette
are unchanged. The reported disappearance was not reproduced in headless Chrome
before this change, so a browser compositing cause remains unconfirmed.

Shared Premium button shines now use a six-second cycle: a two-second round trip
and four-second rest, retaining the three-second initial delay. Shared pricing
allowance boxes now have a subtle one-pixel outline using `--upgrade-border`,
including dark mode. These outlines intentionally change the pricing visuals
without changing box dimensions. Existing screenshot references remain fixed.

Verification: the disposable landing, rendered ring, public visual, primary-action
and Premium-upgrade suites passed 68 checks with eight viewport/hover skips.
Ring captures cover 1440px, 1100px and 768px, both direct theme loads, repeated
switching during sending, paused and completed states, reduced motion and the
View Transition fallback. Captures are in `/tmp/mailloop-ring-shine-after`;
all public references passed without update mode. TypeScript, changed-file lint,
formatting, color and whitespace checks passed. The runner cleaned up its
disposable database and server.

## Public visual references (2026-11-12)

The current compact public pricing cards and mobile landing layout were reviewed
against the previous references. The mobile landing page is shorter because the
pricing cards use the compact layout; the pricing page retains both plans,
comparison table, fine print and footer. Privacy and terms retain their content
and responsive layout. The user chose to keep this design, so the 28 public
visual references were regenerated with the disposable browser fixture and the
full public visual suite passed again without update mode.

Chalk queued indicators now use bright golden yellow instead of dark amber
(2026-11-10). This intentional palette change covers the batch ring, progress
bar, queued markers and their hover tint; status text retains its darker ink.
Usage allowance bars and queued legend dots share this yellow. Healthy allowance
rings retain Chalk's black ink, and warning text retains its darker amber.
Desktop and mobile progress-card checks passed using the disposable database
runner. Before/after captures are in `/tmp/mailloop-progress-before` and
`/tmp/mailloop-progress-after`; screenshot references were not updated.

Ordinary component layout, spacing, typography, colors, borders and interaction
states belong in Tailwind utilities beside their owning JSX. Reuse the existing UI
components and `cn`; use explicit component variants when shared controls need
different layouts. Keep React components and outgoing email HTML in their existing
roles.

## Rules

- Use the existing semantic variables and Tailwind color mappings. Keep color
  literals in `src/app/theme-tokens.css`; run `npm run check:colors`.
- Write complete utility strings in conditional branches or explicit maps. Never
  construct a utility name from fragments. Use `cn` for conflicting utilities,
  including arbitrary padding/font sizes and important variants.
- Preserve exact measurements, media/container query boundaries, native behavior,
  and reduced-motion behavior. A nearby default breakpoint can change the UI.
- Use `css-hover:` when moving an unconditional CSS `:hover` rule. Existing
  Tailwind `hover:` rules retain their pointer capability condition.
- Keep animation and test hooks stable. Class names generated by CSS Modules are
  implementation details; test semantic controls and visible behavior.
- Use important utilities only where an existing unlayered native/theme adapter
  must be overridden. Do not add global overrides to patch ordinary layout.
- Preserve runtime measurements through CSS variables/inline styles. Avoid large
  `@apply` blocks and long descendant utility chains where a child component can
  own its styles.

## Why CSS remains

The migration removes ordinary styling from JSX consumers rather than targeting a
stylesheet count. The following groups still have responsibilities that need CSS:

| Files                                                                | Responsibility                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `src/app/theme-tokens.css`                                           | Centralized palettes, color literals and appearance-specific theme values.                                                                                                     |
| `src/app/globals.css`                                                | Tailwind setup and semantic mappings, native element behavior, shared focus/autofill/dialog/table cascade, navigation container behavior, help/tutorial and completion motion. |
| `src/app/workspace-theme.css`, `compose-theme.css`                   | Workspace/Compose theme bindings, shared native controls, scoped state and illustration palettes.                                                                              |
| `src/app/preview-highlight.css`, `src/components/compose.module.css` | Scoped editor/preview marks, browser text decoration behavior, personalization and search motion.                                                                              |
| `src/app/appearance-control.css`                                     | Preview palettes, menu/theme view transitions and motion reset. Geometry and option states are utilities in the component.                                                     |
| `src/app/(app)/templates/template-editor.css`                        | Editor content/native input behavior, form-slot cascade, safe-area composition and motion.                                                                                     |
| `src/components/settings/settings.module.css`                        | Theme bindings, native disabled/focus/dialog behavior and responsive navigation marker pseudo-element.                                                                         |
| `src/components/contacts/contacts.module.css`                        | Contacts palettes, native controls/focus, and scoped shared form/import/action-slot adapters.                                                                                  |
| `src/components/history/history.module.css`                          | History palette bindings, responsive semantic-table/grid composition and shared action/status state cascade.                                                                   |
| `src/components/templates/templates.module.css`                      | Library palette bindings, native meter parts, focus/motion and shared control/theme adapters.                                                                                  |
| `src/components/usage/usage.module.css`                              | Usage palettes/font-face, portaled surfaces and native gauge motion.                                                                                                           |
| `src/components/limit-banner.module.css`                             | Decorative stripe, pip/detail/chevron motion and native focus.                                                                                                                 |
| `src/components/ui/Tooltip.module.css`                               | Portaled theme surfaces, arbitrary content links/focus and bubble motion.                                                                                                      |
| `src/components/PricingPage.module.css`                              | Arbitrary action-slot adapters, theme inheritance, native focus/table boundary and card motion.                                                                                |
| `src/components/pricing/pricing.css`                                 | Public theme/root scrollbars, safe-area/native focus and theme transitions.                                                                                                    |
| `src/components/landing/landing.css`                                 | Public palettes, hydration-independent theme painting, complex overlapping hero/illustration responsive compositions and motion.                                               |
| `src/components/landing/lower-sections.css`, `pricing-section.css`   | Section palettes, decorative pseudo-elements, native focus, hover/reduced-motion composition and gutter alignment.                                                             |

When changing a remaining group, identify its consumers and cascade before removing
it. Move ordinary child styles onto children where practical, and delete obsolete
rules/imports after verification.

## Browser fixtures and baselines

Run browsers through `npm run test:e2e` or the disposable runner:

```sh
npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only --browser=public-visual,theme-audit
```

The runner creates and removes a disposable database, provisions the restricted
admin role, and starts its own host Next server with fake Gmail/billing credentials.
Never point these fixtures at the development database or an existing app server.
It accepts `--grep=`, `--grep-invert=`, `--project=`, `--reporter=`, `--output=`, and
`--config=` for focused checks. Only intentional baseline establishment uses
`--update-snapshots`.

The shared browser fixture snapshots and restores the complete initialized
`SystemControl` row after each test, including failed tests. Plan, Gmail, quota
ledger and billing states are explicit. Worker/server timestamps use UTC; browser
local display uses Asia/Kolkata. Free audits cover Lavender/Nightbloom; Premium
covers all four themes. Theme checks inspect required semantic values and variables
actually consumed by the page, including scoped/portaled surfaces.

Workspace baselines were refreshed against corrected fixtures before the styling
batches. Public baselines cover landing, pricing, privacy and terms. Fonts and
hydration settle, animations are controlled, development indicators are hidden and
reset dates/data are fixed. Keep these references fixed during migration; inspect
and repair differences rather than updating snapshots to make a refactor pass.

## Intentional bug-fix differences

- Public pricing cards use a shared heading/badge row and tighter card, allowance,
  and feature spacing on mobile (2026-11-11). Every feature remains visible.
  Before/after captures are in `/tmp/mailloop-pricing-before` and
  `/tmp/mailloop-pricing-after`; all eight desktop card captures are identical.
  Established screenshot references remain unchanged.
- Purple gradient action/ribbon ink and Chalk muted plan text have accessible
  contrast. Solid accent controls retain their separate ink mapping.
- A pricing header that overflowed by7px at320px uses a smaller logo below360px.
- Focused Contacts autofill retains its inset background paint and focus outline.
- The Usage upgrade action retains its intrinsic label width, wraps when needed,
  and uses smaller horizontal padding in the two-column card. The current-plan
  header stacks below a 320px container so Premium fits at 280px. Overflow checks
  cover 659/660/661px and 800/960/1200px without clipping.
- History locked shortlist tooltips retain in-shortlist, unavailable-contact and
  pending-delivery explanations alongside the Premium upgrade link.
- The editor tabpanel is a valid wrapper; the form ID used by Save is preserved.
- Admin retries can read the usage-reset field through the restricted role. The
  regression test requires rollback after failure, retained request IDs and one
  audit record after the successful retry.

## Verification status

Completed 2026-11-03. Final source passes color checks, Prettier, lint, TypeScript,
418 unit tests and the production build. Prior disposable database verification
passed 326 database tests plus the separate 101-test usage suite and backfill dry
run; this continuation made no database or provider changes.

The complete desktop/mobile browser run executed all 516 cases: 500 passed,
4 failed, and 12 retained their existing project-specific skips. The four failures
were the duplicate-warning palette-loading assertion, Free/Premium Usage visual
audits and plan-card overflow. Each was repaired and passed fresh targeted reruns.
Thus all 504 runnable browser cases have passing verification, with no unresolved
failures or new skips. This is a full run plus targeted reruns, not a claim that
one uninterrupted full invocation was green.

Final Free/Premium screenshot audits and both plan-card tests passed together
against unchanged references. Public landing/pricing/policy comparisons passed
on desktop and mobile in the complete run. Coverage includes 320px viewports,
659/660/661px containers, 280px Premium content, both appearances, light/dark,
menus/dialogs/tooltips, keyboard focus, hover/disabled controls, editor tabs,
previews, navigation and reduced motion. Skeleton/media assertions wait for
streamed styles, and mobile editor checks wait for the actual tab controls.
The touch palette check centers its swatch and verifies the hit target before
sending a touch event, avoiding the fixed help launcher.

Evidence:

- `/tmp/mailloop-browser-complete.log`: complete run, 500 passed / 4 failed /
  12 existing skipped; no mobile failures.
- `/tmp/mailloop-browser-final-retests.log`: duplicate-warning retest and Premium
  audit/plan-card passes; the intermediate Free screenshot failure was corrected.
- `/tmp/mailloop-browser-visual-final.log`: final Free/Premium audits and both
  plan-card tests, 4 passed / 0 failed.
- `/tmp/mailloop-pending-last-targets.log`: final desktop/mobile skeleton and
  tooltip lifecycle checks, 6 passed / 0 failed.
- `/tmp/mailloop-unit-verified.log`, `/tmp/mailloop-format-verified.log`,
  `/tmp/mailloop-lint-verified.log`, `/tmp/mailloop-types-verified.log`,
  `/tmp/mailloop-build-verified.log`: final static/unit/build checks.

All disposable browser databases and servers were cleaned up. No screenshot
references were updated during this completion continuation.

## Pricing card redesign (2026-11-03)

Landing pricing, `/pricing`, and the upgrade dialog now reuse
`src/components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx`. Caller-owned actions, authentication,
localized price resolution, monthly billing, allowances and all feature groups
are preserved. The card redesign intentionally changes rounded surfaces, corner
lighting, dot texture, decorative orbs, feature dividers and the inset Recommended
badge. The badge retains `data-recommended-ribbon` as a stable browser hook.
The Recommended label is 11.5px; Premium actions retain their original theme ink.
Decorative pointer lighting is disabled for reduced motion.

Established public screenshot baselines remain fixed. Their pricing comparisons
are expected to differ because of the requested redesign, including vertical
movement of the unchanged comparison and fine-print sections below taller cards.
Do not update those references to hide these intentional changes. Current
four-theme card and dialog screenshots are recorded by `pricing-ribbon.spec.ts`,
`pricing.spec.ts` and the shared upgrade-card tests in `feature-gates.spec.ts`.

## Public pricing matches the upgrade modal (2026-11-04)

`pricing/plan-card.tsx` now owns the card surfaces, stats, compact feature lists,
and feature keys for the upgrade modal, `/pricing`, and landing pricing.
Allowances and saved role shortcut counts come from `lib/plans.ts`.
`PricingCards` retains caller-owned actions and adds current-plan and optional
context props. Public cards never highlight a feature.

Intentional visual changes replace public grouped features with the modal's five
Free and ten Premium rows, dotted surfaces, corner circle, filled checkmarks,
gradient Premium border, and stat tiles. Both public actions sit at the bottom
with consistent sizing. The columns use 1:1.15 proportions from 700px; below
700px Premium appears first. Landing's immediate pricing container uses the
upgrade app surface and tighter section spacing. Whole-card hover translation
has been removed; the restrained pointer spotlight respects reduced motion.
Public pages scroll normally. The modal retains its scrolling body, fixed footer,
context chip, and feature highlighting. Checkout/authentication handlers,
localized price resolution, comparison table, and fine print are unchanged.

Established screenshots remain fixed. Before-change captures are under
`/tmp/mailloop-pricing-before`; new palette, breakpoint, focus, and modal captures
are under `/tmp/mailloop-pricing-after`. These are review artifacts, not replacement
baselines. Browser checks use the disposable database runner.

Stat text uses dedicated `--upgrade-stat-gradient` and `--upgrade-stat-label`
tokens. Nightbloom's figures use a brighter lavender gradient and Obsidian's use
brighter neutral highlights; labels have stronger contrast in every palette.
These tokens affect only allowance tiles, keeping action gradients intact.
All stat text and each gradient endpoint must meet at least 4.5:1 against its tile.

Verification: `/tmp/mailloop-pricing-final.log` records 20 passing focused browser
checks and four intentional skips (the modal's desktop project already runs its
own mobile viewport matrix). Final captures are in `/tmp/mailloop-pricing-final`.
Coverage includes all four palettes, 320px and 699/700px boundaries, stat contrast,
keyboard focus, reduced motion, current-plan badges, and shared sign-in forms.
The earlier broader run also passed localized pricing, hosted checkout retry,
modal checkout retry, feature highlighting, scrolling, and focus-return checks.
It exposed stale button/link and theme-lock assertions, now corrected to verify
existing checkout buttons and theme upgrade dialogs. Four unrelated Contacts
navigation checks still expect a removed “View Premium plan” link; they remain
unchanged. TypeScript, lint, color checks, formatting, and the production build
passed. All disposable test databases and servers were cleaned up.

## Compact workspace footer (2026-11-04)

Signed-in pages select the shared footer's `workspace` variant for both plans.
This intentional presentation change removes the marketing action row, product
columns, tagline and status line. Brand, copyright, support/legal links and creator
credit form one desktop row aligned with the theme-dependent `.page-container`.
Mobile places brand/copyright and creator credit before the wrapping links.
The dust canvas is centered within 480px, caps its font at 112px and reserves 12%
of text height above the word. Landing retains the canvas defaults and full footer;
pricing retains its separate footer.

All 14 disposable browser checks passed in `/tmp/mailloop-compact-footer.log`.
Captures under `/tmp/mailloop-compact-footer` cover all four workspace palettes at
1440px and 390px, plus landing in light/dark. Reviewed workspace heights are 217px
on desktop and 259–263px on mobile. Checks cover container alignment, destinations,
focus outlines, overflow, reduced motion, scroll assembly, live theme recoloring,
route changes and Free/Premium parity. TypeScript, lint, changed-source formatting
and color checks passed. Existing screenshot references were not updated.

Help and contact links now lead to public `/help` and `/contact` pages; FAQ leads
to `/help#faq`. Both reuse the existing policy-page shell and semantic theme
variables, with no new palette. Help covers setup and sending troubleshooting;
Contact displays the existing support address and an email link. All 16 footer
checks passed in `/tmp/mailloop-support-footer.log`. All eight support-page theme
checks passed in `/tmp/mailloop-support-themes-final.log`, covering both pages in
all four themes at 1440px and 390px, with screenshots, no horizontal overflow and
text contrast of at least 4.5:1. Captures are under
`/tmp/mailloop-support-themes-final`. Existing visual baselines remain unchanged.

## Usage plan comparison redesign (2026-11-05)

The current-plan card now places the plan name, subscription status, test-mode
badge, feature chips and billing actions beside daily/monthly limit comparisons.
It stacks at a container width of 860px or less. All new presentation uses
Tailwind utilities and the existing four-theme tokens. The obsolete
`usage/plan-card.module.css` has been removed; the shared upgrade-button shine
and its reduced-motion behavior are retained.

Figures and proportions come from `lib/plans.ts`: Free compares 3/20 daily and
15/300 monthly (15% and 5%); Premium shows full bars and “Included with Premium.”
Accessible meters describe plan limits. Live remaining allowances continue to
appear in the existing allowance cards below. Checkout, portal, subscription
menus, tooltips, pending/error states, historical charges, renewal/grace details,
suspension and cancellation retain their existing handlers and conditions.

Intentional visual differences include the plan-name headline replacing the icon
tile and Free price, three feature chips replacing five stat tiles, comparison
bars, fixed readable typography, rounded split surfaces and relocated actions.
The supplied implementation plan describes Option D, but its original image is
not present in this context; the specified structure guides the implementation.
Established screenshot references remain fixed. Before/after review captures are
under `/tmp/mailloop-usage-before`, `/tmp/mailloop-usage-after` and
`/tmp/mailloop-usage-final`. Unchanged allowance/guidance captures were reviewed:
their layout, fonts, colors and copy are preserved. Their page positions change
with the redesigned card height; fractional capture origins and the fixed help
launcher produce pixel differences in isolated captures.

Verification covers Free/Premium desktop and mobile in all four themes,
320px viewports, 280px content, the 859/860/861px container boundary, proportional
and full meters, localized prices, keyboard focus/menus/tooltips, axe contrast,
reduced motion, checkout/portal failures, cancellation, suspension and retained
status after lookup failure. The broader billing run passed 21 of 22 tests; its
one stale upgrade-modal copy assertion was corrected and passed a targeted
rerun alongside all three card checks. The action check also had an existing
public-pricing link selector corrected to its current button role.
Its public gradient assertion now matches the existing 135-degree pricing
gradient; the complete four-theme/three-width action matrix passed in
`/tmp/mailloop-usage-actions-verified`. All 23 distinct selected browser checks
have passing results across the broader run and targeted reruns. All disposable
databases and host test servers were cleaned up.
TypeScript, lint and the application color-literal check pass. Browser runs use
disposable databases with fake provider credentials; no production data, schema,
authentication, API or billing-service code changes.

## Checkout confirmation redesign (2026-11-05)

The verified return state now uses a rounded, bordered card without an outer
shadow, a checkmark tile and Premium/Test Mode badges, three equal desktop billing
tiles, shared Premium allowances, and ordered Usage/management/cancellation
actions. The divided footer distinguishes the stored recurring charge before tax
from the advertised regional price and retains refresh and support controls.
Mobile stacks the tiles and wraps actions, including at 320px. Existing semantic
tokens support Lavender, Nightbloom, Chalk and Obsidian without new color literals.

The success card is gated by the existing verified settlement and period checks.
Suspended and Free access use “Payment confirmed” with their actual current access
instead of claiming Premium access. Override, suspension, cancellation, grace,
configuration and lookup/error notices remain visible. Polling, refresh, portal
and cancellation handlers are unchanged. Pending, timeout, failed and expired
states retain their previous presentation and their return link; the confirmed
card owns its single primary “Back to Usage” action.

These are intentional confirmation-state visual changes. Image #1 was not
available in this implementation context, so the supplied plan governed the
layout; an exact image comparison was not possible. Existing screenshot baselines
remain fixed. Reviewed card captures for all four palettes at desktop and 320px,
plus 390px review artifacts, are under `/tmp/mailloop-confirmation-browser`.

Verification: all 48 desktop/mobile billing browser checks passed in
